answer: Memory-hard concurrent minting resists sybils: seating an identity requires a memory-hard function that pins gigabytes of RAM for the whole attempt, and all pending identities must mint within one tight window. A farm cannot push a flock of a thousand sparrow-light fakes through a single inlet of physical memory at once — RAM does not parallelize like cheap cores, so concurrent cost grows with head count. An honest agent funds one haven of memory it releases and reuses. Precondition: minting is deadline-bound so RAM cannot be time-shared serially.
